Arbitrum Security Council Takes Emergency Action to Transfer Binance-Related Stolen Funds to an Intermediary Frozen Wallet The Arbitrum Security Council announced that it has taken emergency action to rescue 74,559,805 ARB and 8,425 ETH held in an address on Arbitrum One identified as connected to the Binance exploit. The Security Council acted after weighing its commitment to the security and integrity of the Arbitrum community and Arbitrum governance, without impacting any Arbitrum users or applications. After significant technical diligence and deliberation, the Security Council identified and executed a technical approach to move the funds to safety without affecting any other chain state or other Arbitrum users. As of October 30, 2026, the funds have been successfully transferred to an intermediary frozen wallet. The funds are no longer accessible to the address that originally held them and can only be moved by further action of the Security Council or a vote of Arbitrum DAO governance, which will be coordinated with relevant parties. — link

Strategy Reports $19.53 Billion in Q3 Net Income, Sells $432 Million in Bitcoin in 2026 Strategy reported $19.53 billion in net income for Q3 2026, compared with $2.79 billion a year earlier, largely driven by $20.91 billion in digital asset gains. The company also disclosed that it sold approximately $431.8 million worth of Bitcoin year-to-date to fund a portion of its preferred stock dividends and STRC share repurchases. As of October 25, Strategy held 848,517 BTC, up 26% year-to-date, having purchased $14.33 billion worth of Bitcoin during 2026. CFO Andrew Kang will step down on November 5, with Reza Virasteh set to succeed him on January 1, 2027. — link

Binance Says $6.3B Security Incident May Stem From Compromised DevOps Laptop, No Evidence of Private Key Leak Binance said its initial investigation suggests the security incident may have involved a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, allowing the attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. The exchange said it has found no evidence that any wallet private keys were leaked. Binance estimates the total impact at approximately $6.3 billion, with around $3 billion in affected assets frozen on-chain. Deposits and withdrawals have been temporarily suspended, and the affected address authorization has been revoked. Binance said it will cover all losses through its SAFU fund and company funds, with a detailed technical post-mortem to follow. — link

Blockaid Reveals How Hacker Took Control of Binance Wallet: One of 50 EIP-7702 Authorizations Succeeded According to analysis by blockchain security firm Blockaid, the attacker used Ethereum’s EIP-7702 authorization mechanism to attack Binance’s Binance 14 hot wallet. Because the attacker could not determine the hot wallet’s live nonce, and EIP-7702 authorizations must match the account’s nonce at the time of transaction execution, the attacker submitted 50 authorizations with different nonces (18914775 to 18914824) in a single Type-4 transaction. Only one matched successfully, allowing the malicious delegation to take effect. The successful authorization delegated the hot wallet’s account code to an unverified malicious asset-transfer contract. The contract allows only the address designated by the attacker to execute the sweep() function, which can transfer ETH and ERC-20 tokens from the wallet while retaining 1 ETH for gas fees. Subsequent incoming assets may also be at risk of being transferred. — link
